title: Orchestration Lanes and Capacity Gating Playbook for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Purpose: Create a concise, actionable playbook that defines 'orchestration lanes' (priority lanes) and capacity gating rules for coordinated launches across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. This playbook will be the canonical runbook used by PMs, Eng leads, and SRE during release trains, helping teams sequence cutovers, reserve buffer capacity, and automate gating decisions to avoid noisy failures and customer-impacting incidents.

Scope: runtime (model servings, batching, KV cache changes), console (dashboards, rollout UI), and API (rate limits, traffic routing). Excludes upstream infra provisioning (cloud provider commits) — those remain the responsibility of Infra/Capacity teams but are referenced in the handoff checklist.

Goals and success metrics:
- Zero Sev1 customer-facing regressions attributable to release timing miscoordination during first 3 coordinated trains using this playbook.
- Average time-to-detect a release-induced latency regression < 8 minutes using preconfigured dashboards and alerts.
- < 10% over-provisioning of Dedicated capacity for launch windows (measured vs forecast).

Core deliverables:
1) Orchestration lane definitions: Green/Yellow/Red lanes with explicit acceptance criteria and which teams may schedule in each lane (e.g., Green: low-risk UI & docs; Yellow: model config changes; Red: runtime kernel/latency-affecting changes).
2) Capacity gating matrix: thresholds and automated checks (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, tail-CPU on GPU hosts) that must pass before next cohort is opened.
3) Launch calendar template: pre-filled timeline for a 6-week train with checklists and ownership fields.
4) Automation playbook snippets: GH Actions / PagerDuty runbook triggers, Slack alert templates, and a small rubric for auto-rollbacks via feature flags.
5) Observability dashboard templates: per-surface launch page, model-level latency heatmap, cohort-level error deck, and an SLO gating dashboard.

Plan / timeline:
- Week 1 (now -> 2026-02-21): Draft lane definitions and the capacity gating matrix. Stakeholders: Aisha, Marcus, Lina (SRE), Jonah (Runtime ENG lead).
- Week 2: Iterate with Console and API PMs; produce dashboard wireframes and a preliminary GH Action prototype for gating checks.
- Week 3: Run a dry-run on internal staging train (console + API feature toggles + runtime model variant), collect telemetry, refine thresholds.
- Week 4: Publish playbook to Confluence, announce to GTM and Eng leadership; schedule 2 training sessions.

Key decisions made so far:
- We will use cohorted rolling windows of 10% traffic by default with 30-minute observation windows between steps. Rationale: balances speed of rollout with ability to detect regressions quickly in time to rollback.
- Primary gating signals are p95 latency, request error-rate, and GPU host tail CPU. Secondary signals include KV cache hit ratio and batching efficiency.
- Canary cohorts will be regional (US-West first) for customers using Dedicated; Hosted API runs global canaries with regional fallback policies.

Open questions / risks:
- How to version the gating thresholds per-model vs global? (Action: decision required from Runtime research by 2026-02-25.)
- Integration with Dedicated autoscaling contracts — how much buffer can we programmatically reserve without breaking commitments? (Dependency on Sales/Revenue ops for contract constraints.)
- Risk of alert fatigue if thresholds are too tight. Plan to use anomaly-detection smoothing and a 2-stage alert escalation.

Relevant links and artifacts:
- Draft playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/inference/launch-orchestration/pm-99123
- GH prototype for gating checks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-gates/pull/34
- Staging train telemetry dashboard (internal Grafana): https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/launch-train/staging-launch-99123

Next steps (owner):
- Aisha: finalize lane definitions and publish lane owner roster (due 2026-02-22).
- Lina (SRE): prototype automated gating check and alert flows (GH PR by 2026-02-28).
- Runtime ENG: provide model-level baseline p95 for top-10 flow types (data by 2026-02-25).

Acceptance criteria for marking Done:
- Playbook published and linked in the release calendar template.
- Automated gating check implemented for at least 2 signals and wired into Slack/PagerDuty.
- Successful dry-run executed with notes and threshold adjustments captured in the playbook.

Notes from initial review meeting (2026-02-18):
- Console PMs asked for a separate UI checklist to avoid accidental UI-only releases landing in Yellow/Red lanes.
- SRE proposed a temporary surge lane to be used only when capacity delta is known and approved by Capacity CoE.

Longer-term ideas (beyond scope):
- ML-driven dynamic gating thresholds that adapt to traffic seasonality.
- Integration with billing to compute cost impact of reserved buffer capacity per launch.
